::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
# Genetic Data Analysis for Plant and Animal Breeding

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## 1. Linear Mixed Models

### Mixed Models VS Traditional ANOVA:

$y_{ijk} = \mu + L_i + B(L)_{ij} + G_k + GL_{ik} + \epsilon_{ijk}$

where:
- $y_{ijk}$ = observed value of the trait for the $k^{th}$ genotype in the $j^{th}$ block of the $i^{th}$ location
- $\mu$ = overall mean
- $L_i$ = effect of the $i^{th}$ location (fixed effect)
- $B(L)_{ij}$ = effect of the $j^{th}$ block within the $i^{th}$ location (random effect)
- $G_k$ = effect of the $k^{th}$ genotype (fixed effect)
- $GL_{ik}$ = interaction effect between the $i^{th}$ location and the $k^{th}$ genotype (random effect)
- $\epsilon_{ijk}$ = random error term associated with the $ijk^{th}$ observation, assumed to be normally distributed with mean 0 and variance $\sigma^2$.

Representation of a normalized 3D plot of the mixed model equation:
```{r}
library(plotly)

# Define the mixed model function
mixed_model_function <- function(L, B, G, GL) {
  mu <- 0  # Overall mean
  return(mu + L + B + G + GL)
}
```
